Detailed method

One open tin holds this batch. Currently 500 g flour, 65% hydration, 2% salt, and 1% yeast. That is 325 g water, 10 g salt, and 5 g yeast, 840 g of dough. Currently 1 loaf of 840 g. Smooth the top and proof until the dome clears the rim. The crumb stays close enough to slice. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 325 g water, 10 g salt, and 5 g instant yeast, then knead 8 to 10 minutes until smooth. At 65% the dough is soft and holds a ball. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 60 to 90 minutes. With 1% yeast it should about double.
  3. Shape Pat the 840 g dough into a rectangle, roll it into a log, and pinch the seam. Set it seam-side down in a greased loaf pan. The default 840 g uses a loaf pan about 23 cm long, 13 cm wide, and 7 cm high. If you change the amount, use a pan sized to fit, or split the dough. This batch is 1 loaf. Oil for the pan is extra and is not in the gram total.
  4. Proof Cover the pan for 40 to 60 minutes, until the dome rises above the rim and springs back slowly when you press it.
  5. Bake Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Bake 30 to 38 minutes, until the crust is golden and the sides feel firm.
  6. Cool Turn it out and cool on a rack for at least 1 hour before you slice. The photo shows the close crumb on the cut face of the front slice.
